analysis: The only change in this PR is at line 117 of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Models/GLM5Next/GLM5NextManagedLoadTests.swift. It adds "<think>": 4 and "</think>": 5 to the synthetic tokenizer vocabulary in GLM5NextManagedFixture, which is test-only code. The fixture already writes generation_config.json with eos_token_id [2,4], and the test exactPlanRetainsAllPartitionsAndRawTemplateIdentity expects eosTokenIDs == [2,4]. Token id 4 therefore now exists in the vocabulary, which keeps the fixture consistent with those expectations. I saw no change to production code, and the fixture writes only to temp or isolated directories. The fixture does not touch real model weights, keys, attestation, coordinator protocol or the cache storage path (T-041). Nothing here changes provider authorization, decryption, or the TB-002, TB-007 or TB-011 boundaries. The base_text units (:3 and :4) are unchanged context, and the head unit (:5) shows the single-line vocabulary edit. I found no security regression, no new attack surface and no gap in the threat model. Not verified: whether the production tokenizer or template code handles the <think> tokens safely, since that source was not supplied. This is test-only context and not a security conclusion.
